title: Acceleration of Small Bowel Motility Assessed by Cine MRI
author: Akitoshi Inoue
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.k4gcytw

steps.title: Recruit eligible healthy volunteers
steps.instruction: Enroll ten healthy men (mean age 39.1 years, range 25–53; BMI 23.2 kg/m², range 20.3–26.7) who have no gastrointestinal disease, no history of abdominal surgery, and no contraindications to MRI.

steps.title: Implement fasting and fluid restriction
steps.instruction: Ask volunteers to fast for 6 hours; prohibit fluid intake for the last 2 hours of the fasting period.

steps.title: Administer test substance double‑blind
steps.instruction: Give each volunteer 5 g of either TJ‑100 (dai‑kenchu‑to, Tsumura, Tokyo, Japan) or lactose (“Hoei,” Pfizer, Tokyo, Japan) wrapped in a wafer, with eyes closed to block visual and gustatory cues; preparation is performed by a controller not involved in MRI evaluation to ensure double‑blind conditions.

steps.title: Wait 20 minutes post‑administration
steps.instruction: Allow a 20‑minute interval after the wafer is swallowed before any further procedure.

steps.title: Ingest water to distend small bowel
steps.instruction: Have the volunteer drink 1200 mL of tap water to distend the small intestine.

steps.title: Schedule second MRI session ≥1 week later
steps.instruction: Arrange a second MRI examination on a separate day at least one week after the first; administer the opposite substance (TJ‑100 or lactose) using the same preparation protocol.

steps.title: Position volunteer and acquire localizer images
steps.instruction: Place the volunteer prone on the table of a 1.5‑T MRI system (Signa HDx, GE Healthcare) equipped with an 8‑channel body array coil; have the subject hold breath after inspiration. Acquire coronal FIESTA localizer images (TR 3.4 ms, TE 1.1 ms, flip angle 75°, slice thickness 10 mm, matrix 256 × 256, FOV 450 mm) of the entire abdomen and select the slice that shows the maximum length of the small bowel for subsequent cine imaging.

steps.title: Perform cine MRI scans at specified time points
steps.instruction: Using the same FIESTA parameters as the localizer, acquire three successive coronal cine scans (70 images over 35 s each) in the selected plane at each of the following times after water ingestion: 0, 10, 20, 30, 40, and 50 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Set the scanner to the FIESTA sequence (TR 3.4 ms, TE 1.1 ms, flip angle 75°, slice thickness 10 mm, matrix 256 × 256, FOV 450 mm).
At each time point, run the cine acquisition three times, each producing 70 images in 35 s.

steps.title: Conduct image analysis and contraction counting
steps.instruction: Two radiologists (9 yr and 32 yr GI experience), blinded to the administered substance, reach consensus to: (1) select a single jejunal loop in the left upper abdomen and a single ileal loop in the right lower abdomen that remain in the slice throughout the scans; (2) visually count contraction events in each loop for every cine series, assigning 1 for a full contraction cycle and 0.5 for a half contraction; (3) sum the counts from the three scans for each phase.

steps.title: Compute means and perform statistical tests
steps.instruction: Average the summed contraction frequencies and distention scores across all ten volunteers for each time phase. Compare TJ‑100 versus lactose using the Wilcoxon signed‑rank test; assess correlation between total contraction frequency and distention score with Spearman’s rank correlation. Conduct all analyses with SPSS Statistics 22 (IBM) and consider P < 0.05 statistically significant.

steps.title: Apply contraction and distention scoring criteria
steps.instruction: Define contraction scores: full contraction = 1, half contraction = 0.5. Define distention scores (0–2) based on the proportion of loops filled with high‑intensity fluid on MRI: 0 = <30 % dilated, 1 = 30–70 % dilated, 2 = >70 % dilated.
